about.title: Sonora Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Sonora is a small community, and many residents rely on a limited number of local clinics, urgent care centers, and the regional hospital network for treatment. When a provider's error causes serious harm — a missed diagnosis, a surgical mistake, a medication mix-up — patients are often left with more questions than answers. California law sets specific rules for these claims, including short filing windows and a required notice period before a lawsuit can even be filed. LawProactive is not a law firm; we're a free service that connects injured Tuolumne County residents with an independent attorney experienced in medical malpractice matters. That attorney can review your medical records, determine whether the care you received fell below the accepted standard, and explain your options. There's no obligation to move forward, and no fee unless your case results in a recovery. If something about your treatment in Sonora didn't feel right, it's worth having a professional take a closer look.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Wait

items.title: Filing Deadlines Are Short and Strict
items.desc: California generally allows one year from when you discover the injury, and no more than three years from when it occurred, to bring a claim. Waiting to explore your options can permanently affect what you're able to recover.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Period Applies
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed in California, the provider must typically receive 90 days' written notice. Getting this step right requires early attorney involvement, not last-minute action.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: California law generally requires a qualified medical expert to support a malpractice claim. An attorney working with your case can help identify whether the standard of care was met before moving forward.

items.question: Does a bad medical outcome automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that medicine involves risk, and a poor result alone doesn't establish malpractice. What matters is whether the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, which is why a qualified medical expert's review is almost always required.

items.question: I live outside Sonora but was treated at a facility here — can I still get help?
items.answer: Yes. Many Tuolumne County residents travel to Sonora for medical care, and where the treatment happened, not just where you live, is what matters for these claims. LawProactive can still connect you with an attorney familiar with claims tied to this area.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: California law caps non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases, though that cap rises each year under current law. An independent attorney can walk you through how this applies to your specific situation and what other types of damages may be available.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after your initial conversation.
